articles.title: Why Your Docker Container Takes 10 Seconds to Stop: PID 1, Signals and Graceful Shutdown Explained
articles.excerpt: Bài "Docker is weird" đang hot trên Hacker News làm mình nhớ lại một chuyện cũ. Team mình từng mất gần một tuần để tìm hiểu vì sao mỗi lần deploy, request lại bị lỗi 502 lẻ tẻ, còn docker compose down…
articles.body: Bài "Docker is weird" đang hot trên Hacker News làm mình nhớ lại một chuyện cũ. Team mình từng mất gần một tuần để tìm hiểu vì sao mỗi lần deploy, request lại bị lỗi 502 lẻ tẻ, còn docker compose down thì lần nào cũng "đứng hình" đúng 10 giây. Hóa ra lỗi không nằm ở code business mà ở một chi tiết rất nhỏ: process của app đang chạy với PID 1 trong container và không hề nhận được signal tắt . Bài này mình giải thích vì sao chuyện đó xảy ra, cách kiểm tra trong 30 giây và cách fix đúng cho cả Dockerfile lẫn code ứng dụng. docker stop thực sự làm gì? Khi bạn chạy docker stop (hoặc docker compose down , hay Kubernetes xóa một Pod), quy trình diễn ra như sau: Docker gửi SIGTERM (hoặc signal khai báo trong STOPSIGNAL ) tới PID 1 của container. Docker chờ hết grace period, mặc định là 10 giây .

articles.title: Let the model write, not compute: lessons from an MCP coach
articles.excerpt: Short answer In GymRap, my personal strength coach, the language model never produces a number. A Cloudflare Worker computes every score and target in tested code; ChatGPT connects to it as a remote M…
articles.body: Short answer In GymRap, my personal strength coach, the language model never produces a number. A Cloudflare Worker computes every score and target in tested code; ChatGPT connects to it as a remote MCP server, reads a structured brief and writes only the coaching text, which the server validates against a schema before storing. The server, not the model, guarantees the daily report: when the model's write does not arrive, a numbers-only report still goes out, and an uncertain email is never sent twice. The split: numbers in code, words from the model GymRap reads what my watch and phone record through Health Connect: 23 record types, uploaded by a small Kotlin bridge only for the days that changed.

articles.body: OpenAgentForum (openagentforum.com) is a message board where every participant is an AI agent and every message is a signed envelope. I have been auditing its public channels for a few weeks, and this time I looked at something different: governance. The forum supports polls, and its first community poll ran in early September. Instead of trusting the reported result, I recomputed it from the raw record, seven weeks after it closed. What the poll was. "What should this network build next?" - opened Sep 2, 2026 by the agent ClaudeFable, closed by deadline on Sep 4. Four options, numbered from zero: (0) relay identity and signed receipts, (1) wake hooks for reactive agents, (2) a second archive with archive-to-archive comparison, (3) threaded conversations.

articles.body: Originally published on Loop & Retry — field notes on building LLM agents that survive production. This cluster has spent four posts on how a crew of agents breaks. Split-brain is two agents writing to a shared store from different baselines. Goal drift is the objective decaying one handoff at a time. Context drift is the crew's beliefs about a fixed objective going stale unevenly. Observability for multi-agent systems is how you see any of it happening, on top of the four modes in failure modes in multi-agent teams . Read the remedies at the end of those posts and a pattern shows up.

The decision for you is whether that boundary, with your application owning business permission, fits your onboarding task well enough to try a sandbox integration. The problem: one status, three questions A status such as Approved answers a narrow question about provider evidence.

articles.body: MiniMax M3.1 Flash: How a 428B MoE Model Cuts Agentic AI Costs by 70% Without Sacrificing Performance MiniMax released M3.1 Flash on October 19, 2026, and the numbers are hard to ignore: a 428-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model that activates only 23 billion parameters per token, runs at over 200 tokens per second, and costs $0.15 per million input tokens — roughly 70% cheaper than its predecessor. But the more interesting story is in the engineering choices that make those numbers possible. The MoE Arithmetic: 428B Total, 23B Active Mixture-of-Experts architectures have become the dominant approach for scaling language models without proportionally scaling inference cost.

articles.title: MCP subscriptions/listen: change notifications without the surprises
articles.excerpt: Opening a stream is easy. Keeping it useful when connections drop and your server runs across multiple instances? That's where things get interesting. 😅 I just published a practical walkthrough of su…
articles.body: Opening a stream is easy. Keeping it useful when connections drop and your server runs across multiple instances? That's where things get interesting. 😅 I just published a practical walkthrough of subscriptions/listen in the 2026 Model Context Protocol (MCP) specification. What you'll learn How subscriptions work: Open a long-lived stream and request the notification types you care about. Why acknowledgements matter: The server acknowledges the subscription before sending notifications. What notifications actually tell you: They're signals that something changed, not the updated resource itself. How reconnects work: Missed events aren't replayed, so clients need to subscribe again and refresh their state.

articles.title: Never finishing the fight: Where did Xbox go wrong with Halo?
articles.excerpt: After a failed soft reboot and a remake of the original, the Halo universe is facing yet another major creative shift. But has Xbox learned any lessons this time?
articles.body: Halo: Campaign Evolved was Xbox’s second attempt at refreshing the 2001 sci-fi FPS classic, and it is perfectly fine. A cromulent remake, if ever there was one, but it’s hardly a franchise-saver, especially as Xbox looks to rethink its studio structure and approach to renowned IPs like Halo or Gears of War . Halo hasn’t been the same since original developer Bungie — now owned by Sony and working on Destiny and Marathon — departed, leaving 343 Industries (now Halo Studios) to guide the franchise. Neither Halo 4 nor 5 meaningfully evolved the gameplay formula or overarching narrative. Halo Infinite found more success by reheating what “old Halo felt like” and sticking it into a half-baked open world, but it still felt far from the series’ glory days.

At NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, Voyager Technologies' Griffin Mission One (or Griffin-1 ) lunar lander has gone through an absolute gauntlet of tests. articles.title: 'Stupendously large black holes' aren't a major component of dark matter, study finds
articles.excerpt: Black holes more massive than entire galaxies are not a major component of dark matter, the mysterious stuff that's thought to make up most of the matter in the cosmos, a new study finds.
articles.body: Black holes more massive than entire galaxies are not a major component of the mysterious dark matter that's thought to make up most of the matter in the cosmos, a new study finds. For decades, to explain why galaxies do not spin apart at the speeds at which they whirl, scientists have suggested the existence of an unseen substance known as dark matter , whose gravitational pull helps keep galaxies together. Dark matter is thought to make up about five-sixths of all matter in the universe . Much remains unknown about dark matter, however — including whether or not it actually exists. Black holes make good potential contenders for dark matter, since they are extremely massive and are difficult to spot in the dark depths of space.

articles.title: Rocket Lab launches 3 'Hawk' satellites to orbit to gather signals intelligence
articles.excerpt: Rocket Lab launched a trio of private signals-intelligence satellites to orbit today (Oct. 21), the 19th mission of the year for the California-based company.
articles.body: Rocket Lab launched a trio of private signals-intelligence satellites to orbit today (Oct. 23). The mission lifted off aboard an Electron rocket from Rocket Lab’s New Zealand launch site today at 3:11 a.m. EDT (0711 GMT; 8:11 p.m. local time in New Zealand). The Electron carried three "Hawk" satellites for the Virginia-based company HawkEye 360, which explains the name Rocket Lab gave to the mission: "We're Not Hawking Around." If all goes according to plan, the three Hawks will be deployed into low Earth orbit (LEO), at an altitude of 323 miles (520 kilometers). Once up there and commissioned, the satellites will scan the globe for radio frequency (RF) emissions.

articles.title: Space debris: Are we on track for true sustainability? (op-ed)
articles.excerpt: Space is a critical infrastructure layer, underpinning nearly all systems that enable modern life as we know it. It’s therefore critical to maintain a safe and clean orbital environment.
articles.body: David Zamora is the chairman of the Space Data Association. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . The commercialization of space is well underway, and as a result, Earth’s orbit is becoming ever more congested. The current number of active satellites in orbit stands at around 16,000, according to the European Space Agency( ESA), and this number is expected to jump close to 60,000 by 2035, Novaspace projects . While it’s not always given the recognition it deserves, space has fast become a critical infrastructure layer, underpinning nearly all systems that enable modern life as we know it. Therefore, it’s critical that a safe and clean operating landscape is maintained.
